content: A pinguecula is a common, benign growth that develops on the conjunctiva, which is the mucus membrane covering the white part of the eyeball and the inner surface of the eyelids. A pinguecula typically appears as a small, yellowish nodule on the conjunctiva near the cornea. It can develop on either side of the cornea but is more commonly found on the nasal side. Over time, it may gradually increase in size, often over the course of many years. The exact cause of a pinguecula is not fully understood. However, chronic exposure to sunlight, particularly ultraviolet (UV) light, and irritation of the eyes are thought to be contributing factors in its development. Individuals at higher risk for developing a pinguecula include those who are frequently exposed to significant amounts of sunlight, such as people living in tropical climates. Eye irritation and certain occupations, such as welding, which may involve exposure to eye-damaging conditions, also increase the risk. A diagnosis of pinguecula is typically made during an eye examination. It is important to distinguish it from a pterygium, which is a wedge-shaped area of fibrous tissue that can grow onto the cornea. Urgent medical care is generally not required for a pinguecula. However, if there are changes in its size, shape, or color, or if it begins to interfere with vision, it is advisable to consult an eye doctor. In most cases, no treatment is necessary for a pinguecula. Artificial tears can be used to lubricate the eyes, and mild steroid eye drops may be prescribed temporarily to reduce inflammation or irritation. In rare cases, surgical removal may be considered to alleviate discomfort. Some individuals may also opt for surgical removal for cosmetic reasons. Conditions with similar symptoms include pterygium, which should be considered during diagnosis. It is unclear whether a pinguecula can be completely prevented. However, avoiding eye irritants and wearing high-quality sunglasses that block harmful UV rays may help reduce the risk of developing this condition. The prognosis for a pinguecula is excellent, as it is a non-cancerous condition.
